title: India launched XYZ on January 15, 2026, at a cost of ₹500 crore.
rawContent: India launched XYZ on January 15, 2026, at a cost of ₹500 crore. The mission was successfully executed by the space authority. The programme is the first of its kind in Asia and was completed ahead of original scheduling.
assessment: Available evidence generally supports the main claim, but some information requires additional review.

whyReasons.text: Multiple sources support the main claim.
Information is consistent with recent reporting.
One source provides conflicting information on total cost.

fullExplanation: Comprehensive multi-source verification confirms the primary event occurred on January 15, 2026, as reported by major international and state agencies. However, financial audit records indicate an updated expenditure figure of ₹612 crore rather than the initial outlay of ₹500 crore, creating a slight discrepancy in financial assertions.

recommendation.headline: REVIEW BEFORE SHARING
recommendation.description: Most available evidence supports this claim, but one important detail conflicts with another source.
nextSteps: Check the ₹500 crore figure against the latest budget revision document.
Note that the launch date and operational status are fully confirmed.
Share with contextual clarification regarding phase-one vs total program outlay.

claims.text: India launched XYZ on January 15, 2026.
claims.explanation: Official press releases and independent aerospace trackers confirm the launch took place on January 15, 2026, from Sriharikota.

supportingEvidence.title: Press Information Bureau Release
supportingEvidence.excerpt: The mission was formally deployed on 15 January 2026 with full telemetric validation.

claims.text: The project cost ₹500 crore.
claims.explanation: One government release lists the figure as ₹500 crore, while a later budget document reports a revised total. The difference has not been reconciled in public reporting.

supportingEvidence.title: Press Information Bureau release
supportingEvidence.excerpt: "...total sanctioned outlay for the programme stands at ₹500 crore." — 15 Jan 2026

contradictoryEvidence.title: Budget review document
contradictoryEvidence.excerpt: "...revised allocation reported at ₹612 crore following phase two approval." — 04 Feb 2026

claims.text: The programme is the first of its kind in Asia.
claims.explanation: Similar orbital instruments were deployed by JAXA in 2023 and CNSA in 2024, making this claim technically contested without narrower classification criteria.

claims.text: The mission was successfully executed by the space authority.
claims.explanation: All orbital telemetry confirms payload insertion with nominal solar panel deployment and downlink acquisition.

claims.text: The programme was completed ahead of original scheduling.
claims.explanation: Original 2021 blueprint targeted Q3 2025 before COVID-era deferment, though it beat the revised 2026 target by two weeks.

claims.text: Payload telemetric instruments are functioning within designed operational limits.
claims.explanation: First diagnostic beacons were received by ground stations in Byalalu and Svalbard with zero anomalous alerts.

"Officials said the cost figure covers the first phase only; later phases are budgeted separately."
"Launch confirmed on January 15, with independent reporting from three correspondents on site."

title: Viral video claiming a bridge collapse in Kerala
rawContent: Dramatic footage shared on X and WhatsApp asserting a newly inaugurated bridge collapsed in Kerala due to substandard cement.
assessment: Reverse-video keyframe analysis and local state police verification confirm the footage is from a 2021 industrial demolition in Indonesia.

whyReasons.text: Reverse image matching links keyframes to an overseas demolition from August 2021.
Kerala Police Cyberdome issued a formal clarification debunking the claim.
Multiple regional fact-checkers cataloged the recycled footage.

fullExplanation: The submitted video is recycled archival footage of a controlled bridge implosion from East Java, Indonesia, falsely re-captioned to malign contemporary local infrastructure.

recommendation.headline: DO NOT SHARE — CONFIRMED MISATTRIBUTED FOOTAGE
recommendation.description: This footage is unrelated to any bridge in Kerala. Sharing may contribute to public panic.
nextSteps: Report the viral post on hosting platforms.
Share the Kerala Police Cyberdome clarification in discussion groups.
Refrain from redistributing altered video files.

evidence.excerpt: "The video circulating on social media regarding a bridge collapse is false and shows old foreign demolition footage."
